title: Met refers itself to police watchdog over Meghan letter
description: The Metropolitan Police has referred itself to the police complaints watchdog over its handling of a letter with allegations against Thomas Markle, wh
body: The Metropolitan Police has referred itself to the police complaints watchdog over its handling of a letter with allegations against Thomas Markle, which was handed to his daughter, the Duchess of Sussex, in 2019.The letter, written by Markle's first wife Roslyn Loveless, is believed to have contained claims about Meghan's father.Markle has strongly denied recent allegations that he had possessed images of child abuse, describing them as "sick lies".The force said it had voluntarily referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) "in respect of the decision not to inform other law enforcement agencies, and the decision to pass the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex."The Met added it intended to make further referrals to "relevant overseas law enforcement agencies", a process which it expected to be completed "in the coming days".The letter that will be considered by the IOPC was sent to the Met's royal protection team by Roslyn Loveless, who divorced Thomas Markle in 1975 and died in 2024.The handwritten letter was then passed to Meghan in January 2019, with the duchess saying last week that it had "made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father".Meghan did not provide any details but said it had given her sufficient reason for not visiting Thomas Markle and not allowing him to meet his grandchildren, Archie and Lilibet.Scotland Yard said the letter contained claims about offending outside the UK and that it had been forwarded to "the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness".Confirming that it had referred itself to the IPOC, the Metropolitan Police said it was aware of media reports that it had try to obtain a copy of the letter. "While the letter did not actually contain any information specifically related to security matters, it did contain a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom," it said. It added that the Met has carried out an initial review in recent days which has led to the voluntary referral to IOPC. The watchdog will consider why the Met did not share the contents of the letter with other law enforcement agencies, in the UK or overseas, it contained claims of alleged offences.There are also reports that the Met did not keep a copy of the letter and had to get a copy from the Sussexes.Meghan, in a statement last week, said she believed the allegations in the letter "were being investigated".But the watchdog will have to consider what happened to the warnings.There are also likely to be questions about what royal officials knew about the letter, which was sent when Meghan was still a working royal, and which was forwarded to the Sussexes' office rather than to her personally.Jim Gamble, former head of the Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre, previously told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he would have expected the police to have shared any warnings."If you get information that comes to you about someone from a foreign jurisdiction who represents a threat to children, there's a well-worn path and generally you'd expect a UK police force to share that information," said Gamble."I would have expected the Metropolitan Police to have gone to the FBI to say, 'Look, this isn't proven, it's an allegation, you might want to look at it'. The letter emerged as Thomas Markle's son had told the police in the Philippines about material which was alleged to contain sexual images of children, which he had claimed to have found in possessions belonging to Meghan's father.Thomas Markle had been in the Philippines in December 2025, undergoing hospital treatment, when Meghan wrote to him to end all contact.Authorities in the Philippines have begun investigating the claims. Philippine Police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from Markle's former home.Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes, were handed to police by Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, last week. However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they could examine the items.Thomas Markle Sr has strongly denied all the allegations against him. He has been backed by his daughter Samantha who has dismissed the claims against her father as "fake".

schema.headline: Met refers itself to police watchdog over Meghan letter

title: This Budget was micro and that was deliberate
description: It was not a mini Budget, but it was rather small. It might be called the "micro Budget".Small does not necessarily mean bad, but it clearly falls sho
body: It was not a mini Budget, but it was rather small. It might be called the "micro Budget".Small does not necessarily mean bad, but it clearly falls short of radical action to create a promised new economic model. A new "theory of growth" was not unveiled as promised by the prime minister Andy Burnham.It was preamble, roadmap, consultation, perhaps the starter to the main course, which appears to be the PM's 10-year plan next month.It went unsaid, but the clear stategic aim of Healey's statement was to be the "anti-mini Budget".This "steady as she goes" predictable fiscal event set out to avoid the aftermath seen following Liz Truss's mini-budget, in which unexpected and unfunded tax cuts spooked the bond and currency markets.The markets didn't even flicker on Healey's announcement of £65bn of extra borrowing over the next five years - government interest costs have actually fallen since Wednesday, against the backdrop of market turmoil due to the US-Iran war.The core of the Budget was to get Downing Street through the impacts of the Middle East conflict shock on energy and borrowing costs.If these pressures prove enduring there are some unpalatable decisions that will have to be grasped within the next year. The can will have to be picked up rather than kicked down the road again.It buys more time, more "breathing space", as it were, for the government and the prime minister's long-term strategic plans.On energy, there is some significance to the "cheaper power" mission announced, reshaping what had previously been a focus on clean power. While still committed to Net Zero, a series of technical changes to powers over levies and renewable auctions, will seek to turn the tide on additional pressures on energy costs.On devolution, the plan to allow local mayors to keep some extra business rate and income tax revenues, are more radical than expected. There are trade offs here, but it essentially provides incentives for regional leaders to grow their economies, workforce and tax base, that are normal elsewhere, but have not existed in the UK's very centralised tax system.How the PM will square other aspects of his "theory of growth" with the chancellor's spending constraints is the other significant challenge. Can he announce a 10-year plan without detailing the Liverpool to Manchester high speed train line, or a rebirth of some cancelled HS2 lines he championed a year ago?Away from the long term, the OBR forecast point to a very tricky economic backdrop until the spring, and a trickier spending review, given the need to accommodate the new defence target of 3% of national income by 2030. The PM's insistence he will not call an election for a year are eminently believable given the risk of 5% inflation and declining household income.A "focused" Budget at an uncertain time achieved its narrow aim of a bit of "breathing space" for households and also for the government itself.But the evident gaps in the Budget will need filling in come the PM's upcoming 10-year plan.

schema.headline: This Budget was micro and that was deliberate

title: Burnham says he wants to cut welfare bill 'as soon as we possibly can'
description: The prime minister faced questions about his approach after the Treasury disputed that Chancellor John Healey had suggested to the BBC that the benefi
body: The prime minister faced questions about his approach after the Treasury disputed that Chancellor John Healey had suggested to the BBC that the benefits bill will be cut before the next election, which must be held by August 2029.When Healey was asked by the Today Programme on Radio 4 whether there would be a cut in the bill before polling day, he said: "There will be, there will be a reduction in the benefits bill, we'll do that in a Labour way."But several Treasury sources took issue with this being interpreted as a promise to do so by the next election. Downing Street later said it was "not setting an arbitrary target or timetable".The prime minister's official spokesman would not say whether the government's ambition to cut welfare spending meant reducing it below its current level, or ensuring that future spending rises at a slower rate than is currently projected.Further details about the government's proposals are expected after two major reports are published in November.These include a review of disability benefits co-chaired by Labour minister Sir Stephen Timms and one on young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) led by former minister Alan Milburn.The two reviews were announced by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer after his  attempt to make significant changes to the welfare system, including restricting eligibility for some health-related benefits, resulted in a mass revolt of Labour MPs and an embarrassing climbdown in June 2025.Speaking during a visit to Derby, Burnham said the "big next priority in front of us" is the publication of the Milburn report.He said: "We just want to get stuck into supporting people to help people off benefits and into work. There's no delay there. We want that to happen as quickly as possible."Pressed again for a timeline on his plans, the prime minister said: "We're working hard to cut the welfare bill as soon as we possibly can. But we're doing it in a way that supports people into work."If we just went and made crude cuts, in the end, that leaves people in crisis, and you spend more public money somewhere else, so it's about getting people into sustainable employment."Former Bank of England chief economist Andy Haldane said if the government could provide a plan to show "greater restraint" of the benefits bill, that would "play spectacularly well" with the financial markets.Haldane, who has previously advised Burnham, told the BBC's Political Thinking with Nick Robinson podcast: "If the government could get that through I think it would come with a huge bonus."Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch responded to the Budget by saying the country was "overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed, and drowning in an out-of-control welfare system".Reacting to government briefings and remarks on Thursday related to when a reduction in the benefits bill could take place, Badenoch said it "looks like foot in mouth syndrome is spreading". She said: "Don't let anyone tell you this was a 'do no harm budget'. In doing so little, Labour have harmed our economic security and they've harmed our national security."Welfare spending is forecast to rise this year by £19bn to £353bn. Watchdog and forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said this figure is expected to rise to £431bn in 2031/32, driven primarily by health-related and pensioner benefit spending.Of the figure forecast for 2031/32, £209.8bn is on pensioners, including the state pension and winter fuel payments, while £110.7bn is on universal credit and legacy equivalents and £69.6bn is on disability benefits such as personal independence payments.The government has already pledged to reform the existing state pension triple lock from 2030, and more proposals and changes to the welfare system are expected to emerge in the coming months.

schema.headline: Burnham says he wants to cut welfare bill 'as soon as we possibly can'

title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall
description: People are facing a "painful" and "depressing" few years ahead, economic think tanks have warned, after forecasts showed growth in living standards gr
body: People are facing a "painful" and "depressing" few years ahead, economic think tanks have warned, after forecasts showed growth in living standards grinding almost to a halt.Typical working-age households would see their disposable income fall by £1,050, or 3%, between now and 2029, according to the Resolution Foundation, while the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the current decade would be the worst for household income growth on record.Chancellor John Healey said his Budget offered "breathing space", but said the government could "never remove completely" cost of living pressures.The UK's official forecaster said its latest economic forecast painted a "pretty grim picture".The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), blamed the difficult financial situation facing the UK on higher borrowing costs and inflation caused by the US-Iran war.In response to rising energy prices, Healey has announced measures, including a £100 support payment, aimed at easing pressure on household finances.But that would not be enough to offset the impact of higher energy bills, the Resolution Foundation said."This parliament is increasingly looking like one of two halves," said the think tank's chief executive, Ruth Curtice."The first half has been marked by rising living standards, solid economic growth and extra funding for public services," she said.However, the second half of the parliament would be "tough going", she said.There would also be growing pressure on the government's spending plans over the parliament, Miller added."Spending plans look extremely tight. They don't look to me like plans that this government would want to deliver," she said."Whether or not they are delivered matters because the spending plans underpin the plan to bring down borrowing," she added.Miller said she was left with the impression that Healey was hoping the economy would improve to take the pressure off those spending decisions.Healey, speaking on the BBC's Today Programme, said "economic storms", including the Iran war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, were affecting countries around the world and the government was seeking to help where it could.He said energy bill help would create "breathing space" for most households.Around 20 million households are set to receive the £100 payment based on which council tax band they are in.But Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said the Budget had left the public finances "more fragile" as Healey had reduced the "headroom" or the buffer that the country has between what it takes in revenues and what it spends.Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey said the £100 energy payment would be identified as the best item in the Budget for many people, but said that it was "not good enough" when you considered the "stealth tax rises" that were taking money out of people's pay packets.

schema.headline: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

title: Victims appalled as deadly crush footage included in Call of Duty
description: Thursday marks the fourth anniversary of the crush, which happened when more than 100,000 people went out in Seoul's nightlife district to celebrate H
body: Thursday marks the fourth anniversary of the crush, which happened when more than 100,000 people went out in Seoul's nightlife district to celebrate Halloween.The narrow streets became so tightly packed that people could not move and some were unable to breathe."We cannot help but be appalled that the chaotic and desperate scene, in which many citizens at the site performed CPR to save one another and victims lay on the freezing street, was used as it was to create a scene in a game," the bereaved families said."Using such an event as material for a game made for entertainment is in itself highly inappropriate and senseless," their statement continued. "If the game developer has even a minimum of courtesy and empathy towards the victims, it should take corrective action without delay."Activision did not comment on the request to edit the scene to remove the video from that night. Modern Warfare 4, which was released last week, had already faced criticism for basing the game on North Korea invading South Korea, as the two countries have been technically at war for decades.Fighting stopped in the Korean War in 1953, but the two countries never signed a peace treaty and conflict is a very real worry in that part of the world.At the launch of the game, Call of Duty's chief marketing officer, Tyler Bahl, told Newsbeat: "We have to understand this is entertainment".

schema.headline: Victims appalled as deadly crush footage included in Call of Duty

title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row
description: Image source, Michael Putland/Getty ImagesByKatie RazzallCulture and media editor and Helen BushbyCulture reporterUpdated 1 hour agoThe guitar George
body: Image source, Michael Putland/Getty ImagesByKatie RazzallCulture and media editor and Helen BushbyCulture reporterUpdated 1 hour agoThe guitar George Michael performed with in his 1987 Faith music video has sold for £180,000 at auction, after a row over the sale of memorabilia related to the singer.The guitar was one of more than 30 items auctioned by Sworders from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, Michael's long-time personal assistant. The sale fetched a total of £238,000 excluding buyers' premium.Bailey died in 2014 and the items were sold by her estranged husband Ian Belcher, who inherited them after her death.Gerard Bailey, Siobhan's brother, told the BBC she "would be horrified at the prospect of the auction being held in her name and that her personal, cherished possessions are being sold off to the highest bidder". Sworders and Belcher declined to comment.Sworders described the 32 lots, including signed photographs, invitations to events and presentation CDs and discs, as a "remarkable group of memorabilia from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, George Michael's long-time personal assistant and trusted confidante".Michael grew up in Hertfordshire and shot to fame alongside Andrew Ridgeley in pop duo Wham! He went on to enjoy solo success with hits such as Faith, Careless Whisper, Father Figure, Outside and Fastlove. He died in 2016.'Dishonourable and shameful'Siobhan was in the process of divorcing Belcher when she died, but was legally still married to him. She did not leave a will. Her brother claimed she had started to draw up a will shortly before she died, which would have left the items to her nieces and nephews, but it was not registered.There is no suggestion that Belcher did not have the right to sell the items, because her estate legally passed to him when she died.Bailey said if his sister had lived a few weeks longer, the items would not have passed to Belcher because he would not have been considered her next of kin. In a letter to the auction house seen by the BBC, Bailey said the rest of the family considered the auction a "breach of [Siobhan's] privacy", adding that the use of her name was "disingenuous" and "wholly unethical".He told the auction house that Belcher's "misuse of my sister's name" was "frankly dishonourable", and profiteering from the items was "egregiously shameful".Bailey asked that the auction should not go ahead, or be in Belcher's name rather than Siobhan's.Image source, Pete Still/Redferns via Getty ImagesImage caption, The memorabilia on sale includes signed photographs of Wham! and George Michael on stageSiobhan Bailey began working as Michael's personal assistant in 1984, joining him in the year Wham! had their first number-one hit with Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go.She remained his PA for 20 years, and her brother told BBC News she avoided the limelight and guarded the pop star's privacy, despite the attention of tabloid journalists hoping for stories."I think she was one of the few people George trusted and whose opinion he valued," Bailey said."She was always honest and straight with him. I guess that's why she stayed working for him for so long through the very, very good and not so good times."The guitar was "a gift" to his sister because the singer "thought so much of her", he said.The instrument had a key role to play in Michael's reinvention from teen pop idol to serious solo artist.In the 1987 video for Faith, Michael - in ripped blue Levi's jeans, white T-shirt and black leather biker jacket - strummed the vintage acoustic guitar that he reportedly picked up in a shop in Los Angeles shortly beforehand.Guitarist magazine recently billed it as "arguably the most famous Gretsch Synchromatic in the world".The auction's biggest sales£180,000 - The Rockabilly Rebel guitar from the Faith video, with original hardshell case and leather guitar strap £7,000 - A Queen Five Live EP sleeve signed by Brian May, John Deacon, Roger Taylor, George Michael and Lisa Stansfield£5,000 - A Faith Tour ringbound itinerary from George Michael's 1988 world tour£4,800 - A presentation CD of George Michael's Older £4,500 - A gold disc of Wham!'s Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go£4,200 - A gold disc of George Michael's I Want Your SexOther items on sale included a note written "with love and admiration" from Michael and Ridgeley, an official Wham! photograph signed "To Siobhan (Special...)", and an invitation to Ridgeley's 21st birthday party."I know she was proud of the various personalised gold and platinum discs she got, though she was very modest about it all," Bailey said.Speaking before Thursday's auction, he said "she would never have consented" to it, adding that the sale "breaks my heart"."I think she'd be devastated that something as personal as her Filofax [tour itinerary] and notes from George are up for grabs. It's just so tawdry and contrary to how she was," he said.Siobhan died suddenly and unexpectedly of natural causes at the age of 56. According to her brother, she wanted the possessions to "have remained with her family and we would never have sold".He accused Belcher of deciding "12 years after my sister's death to cash in".Bailey acknowledged that Belcher had a legal right to sell the items but called it "disingenuous" that the sale was being promoted in her name.Sworders auctioneer Guy Schooling told Guitarist, external that Belcher had been traumatised following Siobhan Bailey's death and stored all the items in his garage."[He was later] persuaded that these things couldn't stay in the garage forever because they would have deteriorated," Schooling said.Get our flagship newsletter with all the headlines you need to start the day. Sign up here.

schema.headline: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

title: Russell Brand's wife tells his rape trial he is 'kind and a wonderful father'
description: Warning: This story contains graphic content.Russell Brand's wife Laura has told a court her husband is "caring, kind and a wonderful father to our ch
body: Warning: This story contains graphic content.Russell Brand's wife Laura has told a court her husband is "caring, kind and a wonderful father to our children".The 39-year-old told the jury at his rape and sexual assault trial that "the way he treats me is to know me", adding: "I feel very seen by him... I love him very much."The media personality faces seven charges - three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault. He denies all the charges and has pleaded not guilty.Giving evidence at Southwark Crown Court in London on Thursday, Laura Brand was asked by the defence barrister if her husband respected her when she didn't want to be sexual with him, and she replied: "Yes absolutely."Laura Brand is the daughter of former golfer Bernard Gallacher and sister of TV presenter Kirsty Gallacher. She married Brand in 2017 and they have three children.She told the court she first met him at the Edinburgh festival in 2006, explaining that he took her number and they started a relationship soon afterwards.She said that after his performance: "I went over and said, 'I'm Laura, Kirsty's sister. That was a great show'."He contacted her the next day, she said. When they met, she said they had oral sex, adding: "He might have wanted to have sex but I didn't want to."Laura Brand said she knew before they met that "he liked women", and found out that while they were dating that he had been having sex with others."I wasn't interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people", she said."I was invested, we both had told each other we loved each other, but it was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous."She said she remained friends with Brand while he was married to singer Katy Perry from 2010 to 2012, and got back together with him in 2015.Asked if she was "aware of his promiscuity" during their time apart, she said: "I was very aware of it. I could read about it regularly in the papers, so I was aware of it and he also told me."Turning to their relationship now, she said: "We have a very honest, frank, and clear relationship and marriage."It is one of the most important parts of our marriage, and our relationship has always been honest."The charges against Brand relate to allegations made by six female complainants spanning a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009.The entertainer has displayed little emotion during the course of his trial, but was seen smiling broadly during parts of his wife's evidence.He let out a laugh when she told the court: "We do have many friends and there are colleagues, and we are grateful for those people."Her evidence came a day after the star appeared in the witness box himself.He told the jury the allegations had a "devastating" impact on his relationships with friends and colleagues, meaning they would not touch him "with a bargepole".He also said on Wednesday he had been promiscuous but believes sexual consent is "fundamental, essential, necessary and indeed in many ways more important than sex itself".On Thursday, the court also heard statements from two of Russell Brand's ex-girlfriendsElia Alvarez Diaz said they were in a relationship and lived together for about a year from 1998 to 1999, and described the defendant as "gentle" and "loving".She described him as being "highly persuasive... a complex character" and "exciting to be with"."When I said no, however, he accepted it," she said in a statement.Their relationship ended because he cheated on her repeatedly, she said.Amanda Alguero Alejos told the court in a statement that Brand had also repeatedly cheated on her."He was undoubtedly promiscuous, never in front of me and never when I was around. That was not what mattered to me at the time," she said.She recalled women "circling" around Brand "like birds", even when they were out as a couple.The trial continues, with the jury likely to retire to consider the verdicts on Tuesday.

schema.headline: Russell Brand's wife tells his rape trial he is 'kind and a wonderful father'

title: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say
description: At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city
body: At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians.In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to the railway operator chief, Oleksandr Pertsovsky."But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform" when the drone struck, he said.Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said the incident was a tragedy, adding that a drone hit an electric civilian train.Pictures from the Ukrainian rescue services show a large hole in a platform that is strewn with blurred-out bodies, near a blast-damaged train with smashed windows.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said "the Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."He called for further US, European and G7 sanctions on Russia and repeated his criticism of a controversial deal that was struck earlier this month between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which eased some sanctions on Moscow, allowing the US to import Russian diesel.Elsewhere in Ukraine, two girls aged 15 were killed in a Russian missile attack on the centre of Chernihiv city, in the north of the country, regional head Vyacheslav Chaus said. At least 25 others, including four children, were injured, he added.A day of mourning has been declared for Chernihiv and Dnipro on Friday.In the city of Kremenchuk, in the central Poltava region, three people were killed and 28 injured in a Russian drone attack that hit residential buildings and a school, regional head Vitaliy Diakivnych said.The latest Russian strikes came during efforts to uphold a fragile ceasefire in the besieged city of Oleshky, which has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have been trapped without food, water, medicine and electricity for years.Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, wrote on Telegram that the truce was holding into a third day.Meanwhile, the Kremlin has condemned Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow whilst the city hosts the Russia-Africa Summit, the Tass news agency has reported. The two-day event is attended by African leaders and government delegations from 48 countries.The mayor of Moscow said 613 Ukrainian drones were launched overnight towards the region, most of which were shot down during their flight.Russia's defence ministry has always denied targeting Ukrainian civilians and says its attacks on railways target the infrastructure used to transport military personnel and equipment.However, the dangers to passengers are very real, and attacks on Ukraine's train infrastructure have risen sharply.Of the 521 locomotives hit since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, almost 60% have been hit this year, according to statistics released by Ukrzaliznytsia supplied to AFP news agency. Overall attacks on railway facilities have risen from 1,206 in 2025 to 1,700 so far this year.There appears to have been a wider assault on Ukraine's infrastructure in recent weeks, with two bridges attacked in the capital Kyiv, and a metro train hit during one of the strikes.Additional reporting by Jaroslav Lukiv

schema.headline: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say

title: Michelle O'Neill blocked from PM meeting in Glasgow
description: A meeting of the party's ruling officer committee was held earlier on Thursday.DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the first minister's "arrogance will hav
body: A meeting of the party's ruling officer committee was held earlier on Thursday.DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the first minister's "arrogance will have consequences", but O'Neill accused the party of being "reckless and irresponsible"."Her complaints today that she's frustrated from engaging with the British Prime Minister within the sovereign United Kingdom will so be it because her law breaking must have consequences," Robinson said.O'Neill said the DUP leader's comments were "arrogant and supremacist" adding that the DUP "is consumed with their own internal leadership troubles and divisions".She said she would be at the Assembly on Monday with her party colleagues to "keep showing up every day for people".Earlier she described the move to block the meeting with the prime minister as "reckless and irresponsible" and meant people in Northern Ireland "will not be represented"."This is a reactive stunt, driven by the DUP's own internal pressures and electoral problems," she said in a statement posted online.The prime minister revived the National Economic Council over the summer to encourage greater collaboration between the nations and regions.Earlier Little-Pengelly said the concerns arising from O'Neill's conduct and the "anger and hurt felt by many people across Northern Ireland, cannot simply be ignored or minimised".She said the decision comes after stopping a separate planned engagement with the President of Ireland, Catherine Connolly."I have requested a separate meeting with the Prime Minister to ensure Northern Ireland's interests, including the urgent budgetary and funding challenges facing the Executive, continue to be represented directly," she added.O'Neill and other senior Sinn Féin figures have been interviewed by police investigating last month's unnotified demonstrations in Portadown, with unionists accusing the party of acting unlawfully.The Sinn Féin deputy leader has defended her involvement, saying it was the "right thing to do".The Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV) leader Jim Allister said "the DUP's sham response today was beyond pathetic" adding "the DUP is interested only in clinging to office, not principle".Alliance leader Naomi Long said refusing to attend or preventing others from attending the meeting with the prime minister was reckless and put party interests ahead of Northern Ireland's economic future and the needs of the public.The Ulster Unionist Party leader Jon Burrows told BBC's Evening Extra programme the situation was a "political fudge" that was "all choreography and no consequences," adding that the move would "probably galvanise Sinn Féin further at the ballot box."The Social Democratic and Labour Party's (SDLP) Matthew O'Toole said "plunging this place into more political chaos is not a sensible strategic move for unionism"."Ultimately it's only going to make reasonable people here conclude that the largest unionist party simply doesn't want to make the status quo work," he added. The DUP has been under pressure from unionist rivals and some within its own ranks over how to respond to the row over Drumcree.Last week, DUP MP Carla Lockhart stepped down from the party's officer board over their leader Gavin Robinson not withdrawing Little-Pengelly to force O'Neill from their joint Stormont office.On Thursday Lockhart said she will follow her "own course" if the party does not seek to remove Sinn Féin's Michelle O'Neill as Stormont's first minister.Robinson said that while O'Neill and her party colleagues "should be punished, that does not include punishing the rest of Northern Ireland".The Upper Bann MP, who last week quit the DUP's ruling officer board in opposition to party leader Gavin Robinson's approach, outlined her position in a letter to colleagues which she later posted on Facebook.Other DUP representatives including assembly member Diane Forsythe have since backed Lockhart's calls for O'Neill to be "removed from office".On Tuesday, Forsythe said that in the absence of such "meaningful action", official engagements through the joint Executive Office should be stopped immediately as a "bare minimum".On Wednesday, a second DUP assembly member called for O'Neill to go.Maurice Bradley said removing O'Neill "would not, in itself, require the Assembly to collapse".

schema.headline: Michelle O'Neill blocked from PM meeting in Glasgow

title: Mexico City Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli to miss media day with illness
description: Antonelli is one of two drivers to miss media day with an illness.The other is Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, who his team said was "unwell".A Cadillac s
body: Antonelli is one of two drivers to miss media day with an illness.The other is Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, who his team said was "unwell".A Cadillac spokesperson said: "The team has taken the decision to allow him a day of rest, to support his recovery."This is a precautionary measure and does not currently affect his participation in the remainder of the race weekend. We will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates if necessary."On Wednesday, Cadillac announced a new contract for the Finn's team-mate Sergio Perez, who will stay with the team until at least 2029.They made no mention of Bottas' future in the announcement, and are said by insiders to be considering whether to promote their American reserve driver Colton Herta into F1.Herta is having his fifth outing of the year in practice on Friday at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, as the team seek to earn him enough mileage to secure the so-called super licence that is required to race in F1.Herta, previously a front-runner in the US-based Indycar championship, moved to Formula 2 this year with the intention of preparing himself for F1.His season has not gone well and he is currently 19th in the standings with a best result of fifth place.However, Cadillac feel he has shown more potential in his F1 outings, which also include a number of runs in cars from previous years.No decision has been made on whether Bottas or Herta will partner Perez in 2027.

schema.headline: Mexico City Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli to miss media day with illness

title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Florida on WednesdayByVanessa BuschschlüterLatin America online editorThe defeate
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Florida on WednesdayByVanessa BuschschlüterLatin America online editorThe defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro, has referred to himself as "leader of Brazil" in a letter he published on social media after leaving the country for the United States. Bolsonaro lost to his left-wing rival, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, in the run-off on Sunday by a difference of 4.4 million votes, but has not conceded defeat. In the letter, Bolsonaro alleges, without offering evidence, that he was the victim of "electoral fraud" and says that he will lead the opposition from the US.He left Brazil on Tuesday after failing to comply with an order to surrender his passports, a decision which Lula described as "a shameful act".Figure caption, Watch: Has Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil to evade justice?Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival. In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".The extension was requested by both Lula's and Bolsonaro's campaign teams, and the head of Brazil's electoral authority has said that the vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws and constitution.An analysis of election data conducted by BBC Brazil and BBC Verify has also found that only around 34,000 people voted during the extended hours - far lower than the 4.4 million votes that separated Lula from Bolsonaro.In his letter, Bolsonaro also addresses his departure from Brazil - which caused confusion after he disappeared for more than 24 hours.It later emerged that he had gone across the land border to Argentina, and from there flew on to Florida, following a brief refuelling stop in Ecuador. Bolsonaro left after failing to hand in his passports to police - in defiance of a Supreme Court order, which had been issued as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering.He has not been charged as part of the money laundering probe and denies any wrongdoing, calling the investigation a "politically-motivated witch hunt".Bolsonaro added that he had never intended to leave Brazil, but argued that he was the victim of "political persecution".He ended the letter by saying: "I left Brazil but I haven't abandoned Brazilians".While Flávio Bolsonaro said that he planned to lead the opposition from the US, it was not clear how he planned to do that.His party recognised the election result and while some of its politicians have described Bolsonaro as a "political exile", his campaign manager, Rogério Marinho, stated on Wednesday that "there is no evidence" of the electoral fraud that Bolsonaro alleges took place. It is also not yet clear where Bolsonaro intends to stay or for how long. His younger brother, Eduardo, has been in self-imposed exile in the US since March 2025, saying he was the victim of political persecution. The two siblings posted a photo of themselves holding a Brazilian flag on Wednesday. Image source, Eduardo Bolsonaro/Instagram/ReutersImage caption, Flávio Bolsonaro's brother Eduardo posted a photo of the two of them in the USThe Trump administration has provided visas for Flávio Bolsonaro and his family but did not say what kind of visas they were.The US president did not explicitly endorse Bolsonaro in the run-up to the election and told reporters he "won't get involved" when asked about Bolsonaro's allegations of election fraud. Earlier in the week, he had said that "it looked like another rigged election," without providing any evidence.And on Thursday, Trump told reporters that "the election was a very great embarrassment to the people of Brazil".

schema.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss

title: Arsenal's Max Dowman to miss three matches after red card appeal rejected
description: Arsenal's Max Dowman will miss three matches after an appeal against his sending-off during Tuesday's Carabao Cup loss at Fleetwood was rejected.The 1
body: Arsenal's Max Dowman will miss three matches after an appeal against his sending-off during Tuesday's Carabao Cup loss at Fleetwood was rejected.The 16-year-old midfielder was shown a straight red card in the 85th minute after reacting to a heavy challenge by Fleetwood's Harrison Neal.Although Dowman did not fully kick out, his foot did make contact with Neal.The game finished 1-1 before League Two Fleetwood beat the Premier League champions 5-3 on penalties.Arsenal appealed Dowman's sending-off on Wednesday.It was Dowman's second red card this month having also been sent off while representing England's Under-19s.As Dowman left the field, Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta gave him a scathing look and made what appeared to be an angry comment to the young winger.Arteta said after the game: "When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate. It was very clear."Dowman was dismissed for violent conduct, which according to the laws of the game is when a player "uses or attempts to use excessive force or brutality against an opponent when not challenging for the ball... regardless of whether contact is made".The Gunners were already light on options on the wing as Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke are currently out injured.Arteta's side return to Premier League action away to Liverpool on Sunday.

schema.headline: Arsenal's Max Dowman to miss three matches after red card appeal rejected

title: South Africa vs Australia: Careless dismissals give tourists route to series win
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The winner of the third Test will finish the series top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankingsB
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The winner of the third Test will finish the series top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankingsByMatthew HenryBBC Sport journalistThird Test, Cape Town (day three of five)South Africa 329 & 140-4: Ackerman 62; Starc 2-29Australia 429: Inglis 102; Harmer 4-104South Africa lead by 40 runsScorecardBatters carelessly gifting wickets to Australia... we have been here before.This time it was not England helping their opponents, although they will have taken note with a tour of South Africa to come this winter.South Africa's attempt to fight back in the decisive third Test against Australia was hurt by two poor strokes on day three.Having taken the last six Australian wickets for 99 runs in the morning despite Josh Inglis' second Test century, the Proteas began their second innings facing a deficit of exactly 100.They needed runs from their experienced opener and number three. Neither Aiden Markram nor David Bedingham could deliver.By the end, even captain Temba Bavuma had been tempted into a wild swipe to fall for 35. South Africa were 140-4, just 40 runs ahead, at the close.Australia are closing in.Weakness exposed by AustraliaIn isolation, Markram's drive off Mitchell Starc straight into the hands of mid-off for one appeared the most egregious.The ball was the fullest of the six balls Markram faced but not there for him to play his trademark shot. Fielder Travis Head did not have to move.Worse, though, was the dismissal of Bedingham, who showed he had not learned from the first innings.Then, the right-hander top-edged a pull to Josh Hazlewood off the bowling of Starc. This time he repeated the shot, with Hazlewood the wicket-taking bowler."That is just absolutely soft from David Bedingham," said former South Africa bowler Vernon Philander."He knew they were going to target him in that zone. For the second time in the Test, he has fallen to the same ploy."Image source, CricVizImage caption, The delivery which dismissed Markram was the fullest he had faced but still not full enough to be a driving length Given the prized position in South Africa's batting order on the back of strong domestic form for Durham in the County Championship and twin hundreds for Western Province in September, this score of 11 followed contributions of 49, 46 and 50 in his other four innings.He has got in but has not made a match-winning contribution.Batting in the key position of first drop, some would say that is more infuriating than not getting in at all.His dismissal, again like in the first innings, came shortly after being hit by a bouncer, with Starc clattering one into his chest on this occasion.When, after starting with two balls on a good length, Hazlewood went short again, Bedingham's eyes lit up.Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer and co should have been taking note. It was the fifth time he has been dismissed pulling in his 18 Tests. On average he gets out playing that shot once every 13 deliveries. "He never looks in the right position to play the pull or hook shot," former South Africa captain Graeme Smith said. "He is always off balance. He is never in a strong position."You think about best pullers in the game they have a strong base. He is pirouetting on one leg."[South Africa great] Hashim Amla just put the pull shot away for a phase."That is what a player like Bedingham needs to think about."Cummins tweak brings Bavuma wicketBavuma, in contrast, dug in for 115 balls in which he hit only one boundary.As he had in his 179 in the second-Test win in Gqeberha which set up this grand Cape Town finale, he showed his side the way in a partnership lasting 17.3 overs with Matthew Breetzke after opener Marques Ackerman had briskly made 65 before being bounced out by Starc.But with four minutes to go in the day, Australia captain Pat Cummins tweaked his field for spinner Nathan Lyon.Bavuma had pushed and driven outside off stump to that point but, with a silly point now in place, he was dragged from his crease and tried to force through mid-wicket.Australia's celebrations suggested they believe that was the crucial wicket.The vicious turn Lyon found means any chase over 200 would not be straightforward for Australia. South Africa's spinner Simon Harmer dismissed Inglis and Alex Carey (80) earlier in the day on his way to figures of 4-104.The Proteas have Breetzke and Ryan Rickelton at the crease - and Test triple-centurion Wiaan Mulder to come, before in-form all-rounder Marco Jansen and the tail.This still appears a tall order, however.As on day one and two, Australia have held firm and their opponents faltered. England know that feeling too.

schema.headline: South Africa vs Australia: Careless dismissals give tourists route to series win

title: Sergio Garcia targets Ryder Cup return as he confirms LIV exit to rejoin DP World Tour
description: In his statement, Garcia added that "the most exciting part for me is strengthening personal relationships, both new and old".Garcia was sanctioned by
body: In his statement, Garcia added that "the most exciting part for me is strengthening personal relationships, both new and old".Garcia was sanctioned by the DP World Tour for breaking its rules when he defected to LIV, making him ineligible for the 2023 Ryder Cup.The event's record points scorer had to settle outstanding fines - reported to be more than £1m - in order to be eligible for the 2025 edition, although ultimately he was not selected.After helping Europe to six wins from 10 Ryder Cup appearances, he now hopes to return to their camp at Ireland's Adare Manor next year as a player or vice-captain."Another goal is to make that Ryder Cup team, and to be an asset to the guys in whatever capacity that may be," he said.However, according to the current tour rules, while Garcia is eligible to play again, he cannot serve as a future captain or vice-captain.Garcia may also face an awkward reunion with the PGA Tour.Just before leaving for LIV in 2022, he told a rules official at the Wells Fargo Championship: "I can't wait to leave this tour. A couple more weeks and I won't have to deal with you any more."He has remained eligible to play in majors and after hitting a poor shot at this year's Masters, Garcia ⁠slammed his driver into the Augusta turf and hit a nearby cooler, snapping the ​head ⁠off his club.He apologised at the time and has now added: "There are some great tournaments around the world to play before Augusta next April, and I can't wait to get back to the Masters."I left Augusta last year disappointed with myself and my actions, and I'm ready to show what I've learned and where I am mentally."Augusta has given me some of the greatest moments of my life, and I'd love nothing more than to chase another green jacket at such a special place."

schema.headline: Sergio Garcia targets Ryder Cup return as he confirms LIV exit to rejoin DP World Tour

title: Offshore workers turn to weight-loss jabs to meet new helicopter weight limits
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, New weight rules for travel offshore will come into force in NovemberByRachel BellBBC Scotland NewsReporting
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, New weight rules for travel offshore will come into force in NovemberByRachel BellBBC Scotland NewsReporting fromAberdeen and Calum WatsonBBC Scotland NewsUpdated 2 hours agoHundreds of offshore workers have been using weight-loss jabs to help meet maximum weight rules for helicopter flights due to come into force next week. From Sunday, anyone weighing more than 19st 7Ib (124kg) in civilian clothing and footwear will be banned from taking a flight to an offshore platform covered by UK safety regulations.When the new rules were announced last year, about 2,200 workers were over the limit but that figure has now fallen to fewer than 250, according to Offshore Energies UK (OEUK).The industry body told BBC Scotland News that on one platform, 60% of staff had been taking weight-loss drugs and extra fridge space had been provided to keep the medications cool. The average weight of offshore workers has risen over recent decades, and increased by almost 1st 7Ib (10kg) since 2008. The new weight limit policy came after the Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) warned that rescue winches - which are critical during offshore emergencies - cannot safely lift heavier people.The figure was decided upon after factoring in the weight of the rescuer, stretcher and other kit that would add to the combined total. OEUK health and safety manager Graham Skinner said a range of measures were being used to help offshore workers manage their weight, including gym equipment and healthier food options. Alongside those, he said many had had chosen to make use of the latest medical advances in controlling appetite and digestion. "What we know is that offshore workers are using weight-loss jabs regardless of the policies. Last year we saw in some cases 60% of workers turning up with weight-loss jabs," he told BBC Scotland News."That's brought our average weight down in a very short space of time. I think that's very common in society and it can potentially be a really useful tool if somebody's got a lot of weight to lose it can get them in a good place."He said initially staff appeared to be funding the medication themselves, although he thought it possible that some firms were now supporting them with the costs. Could some workers lose their jobs? The weight-limit policy has been criticised by the RMT union, external which claimed there had been a lack of consultation, and that it could lead to experienced staff being excluded from offshore operations. Earlier this year, BBC Scotland spoke to one occupational health expert in Aberdeen who said some clients were "really stressed" by the new rules while others had chosen to leave the industry. Companies could offer staff alternative onshore roles but Skinner warned: "If somebody has chosen not to lose weight then there's a real possibility they could lose their job."Image caption, Graham Skinner said most offshore workers had managed to get their weight below the new limitHe said there were a number of safety reasons for having weight-limit controls such as working in confined spaces or ability to quickly exit a helicopter - but the actual numbers had been driven by the lifting capacity of the winches."It's the same winch on all search and rescue helicopters and if somebody needs to be rescued due to a health or safety incident the winch has limitations and we can't allow people to exceed those," he said.Workers will be asked to declare if they are under the weight limit and this will be checked at the heliport.He said employers in the industry had been working "really hard" to ensure as many staff as possible complied with the new rules and he hoped the number of staff  over the weight limit could be reduced still further.

schema.headline: Offshore workers turn to weight-loss jabs to meet new helicopter weight limits
